source: Claude draft, 2026-10-13. Not yet checked by a native speaker.

entries.qa: Correct, but さようなら can sound final or formal. Leaving a shop or restaurant, people more often say ありがとうございました or 失礼します; with friends, じゃあね / またね. Reviewer: confirm this is the best card-level choice.
Same word as the existing excuse_me card; すみません is the everyday apology to strangers. ごめんなさい is also common, a bit more personal (friends, children).
Textbook standard and correct; in casual speech people often just say いえいえ (no, no).

entries.target: 大丈夫です、ありがとうございます。
entries.reading: だいじょうぶです、ありがとうございます。
entries.qa: Literally 'I'm fine, thank you': the most common polite way to decline an offer (a bag, a refill). いいえ、結構です is also correct but can sound stiff.
Literally 'Understood.' Neutral, polite agreement. オーケー / はい、大丈夫です are also used.

Literally '(We are) ___, please.' The blank takes a number of people with the people counter (一人 hitori, 二人 futari, 三人 sannin, 四人 yonin), not a bare number; one and two are irregular. Often said in reply to staff asking 何名様ですか？

entries.target: メニューをお願いします。
entries.reading: めにゅーをおねがいします。

entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I have a ___ allergy.' The food word attaches directly as a compound (卵アレルギー = egg allergy). Standard, widely understood. For severe allergies, travellers should also show this in writing and ask about traces; this phrase does not say how severe the allergy is.
Literally 'I am a vegetarian.' Understood, but the concept is applied loosely in Japan: dashi (fish stock) is in many dishes. Clearer add-on: 肉と魚は食べられません (I can't eat meat or fish).

SAFETY. Back-translation: 'With ___ left out, please.' Standard ordering phrase (氷抜き, 肉抜き). ___なしで is an equally common alternative. It is a preference request only: it does not tell staff it is an allergy, so for allergies pair it with allergic_to.

entries.target: 持ち帰りでお願いします。
entries.reading: もちかえりでおねがいします。
entries.qa: テイクアウトで is also common, especially at chains.

entries.reading: てんないでおねがいします。
entries.qa: Literally 'In the shop, please.' Some chains say イートインで.
On leaving a restaurant, ごちそうさまでした (thank you for the meal) is the customary phrase and pairs well with this.

entries.target: もう一つお願いします。
entries.reading: もうひとつおねがいします。
entries.qa: 一つ is the general counter. For a drink, もう一杯 (moh eep-pai) is more precise; for a refill, おかわり.

entries.target: ___までの切符をお願いします。
entries.reading: ___までのきっぷをおねがいします。
entries.qa: Literally 'A ticket as far as ___, please.' In practice the blank is a station name; most tickets come from machines or IC cards.
この電車 (this train) / このバス (this bus) in place of これ is more specific; ___に止まりますか？ (does it stop at ___) is also common.
Literally '(Up) to ___, please': the standard taxi phrase.

entries.target: ここで止めてください。
entries.reading: ここでとめてください。
entries.qa: In a taxi, ここでお願いします is an equally common, softer alternative.

entries.reading: つぎはなんじにでますか？
entries.qa: Literally 'What time does the next one leave?' Clearer with the vehicle named: 次の電車は何時ですか？ (next train) / 次のバス (next bus).
番線 is for train tracks. For buses, ask 何番乗り場ですか？ (which boarding bay).

Direction: '(It's to the) right.' To a taxi driver: 右に曲がってください (please turn right).
Direction: '(It's) straight ahead.' To a taxi driver: まっすぐ行ってください.

entries.qa: Literally 'Could you look after my luggage?': the standard hotel phrasing.

Literally 'I can't use the ___': a general-purpose frame. Japanese prefers a specific verb per item, so the examples use つきません (won't turn on), 出ません (nothing comes out), つながりません (won't connect), 壊れています (is broken).

entries.target: タオルをもう一枚もらえますか？
entries.reading: たおるをもういちまいもらえますか？

entries.qa: Literally 'I'll go with this one.' これください is also common.
Literally 'It's a bit expensive': the natural, softened way to say it. The literal 高すぎます (too expensive) is blunt. Haggling is uncommon in Japanese shops.

ふくろをおねがいします。
entries.qa: Shopping bags usually cost a few yen; staff often ask 袋はご利用ですか？ first.

entries.reading: すこしだけきってください。
entries.qa: Literally 'Please cut just a little.' Salons also say 毛先を整える程度で (just tidy the ends); reviewer may prefer that.

entries.pronunciation_easy: yoh-koh oh mee-jee-kah-meh nee shee-teh koo-dah-sai
entries.qa: 横 (sides); サイド is also used at salons.

entries.target: こんな感じでお願いします。
entries.reading: こんなかんじでおねがいします。

entries.target: ひげを整えてください。
entries.reading: ひげをととのえてください。
entries.qa: Literally 'Please tidy my beard.' Barbers (理容室) usually offer this; many hair salons (美容院) do not.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Help (me)!' / 'Save me!' The standard shout. 誰か！ (Someone!) is also shouted.

entries.target: 警察を呼んでください！
entries.reading: けいさつをよんでください！
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Please call the police!' Police number in Japan is 110; ambulance and fire is 119. A local police box is a 交番 (koban).

entries.reading: いしゃがひつようです。
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'A doctor is necessary.' Clear and understood. In an urgent case, 救急車を呼んでください (please call an ambulance) is what people actually shout; 病院に行きたいです = 'I want to go to a hospital.'

entries.reading: やっきょくはどこですか？
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Where is the pharmacy?' Over-the-counter medicine is mostly sold at ドラッグストア (drugstores), which locals may point you to.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'It's urgent / an emergency!' Understood; 急いでください (please hurry) is a natural follow-up.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I lost ___.' If it was stolen: ___を盗まれました. Lost property goes to the 交番 (police box) or the station's 忘れ物 (lost and found).

entries.reading: たいちょうがわるいです。
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'My physical condition is bad' = I'm unwell. 気分が悪いです ('I feel bad/sick') is also common and leans toward nausea or feeling faint.

entries.target: 電話をかけないといけません。
entries.reading: でんわをかけないといけません。
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I have to make a phone call.' Not fully sure this is the most natural card choice; to borrow a phone, 電話を貸してもらえますか？ (could you lend me a phone?) is more useful in practice.
Literally 'Is there ___?' The standard way to ask a shop or restaurant whether they have something; the noun goes in directly, no article.
Literally 'As for ___, how much is it?' Same shape as the vetted これはいくらですか？

SAFETY. Back-translation: '___ is necessary (for me).' Matches need_doctor, but Japanese rarely says 'I need X' for everyday requests: the examples use what a local would say instead (Please help / Water, please / Please call a taxi). Check that the frame itself reads naturally.

entries.target: この近くに___はありますか？
entries.reading: このちかくに___はありますか？
entries.qa: Literally 'Is there a ___ near here?' The noun goes in directly.
Literally 'Can I pay by means of ___?' Same shape as the vetted カードで払えますか？
The blank takes a verb in its て-form (書いて, 言って), not a noun, because Japanese builds 'could you do X for me' as X-te + もらえますか. Same pattern as the vetted 手伝ってもらえますか？ and もう一度言ってもらえますか？

Literally '___, with ___ left out, please.' First blank is the item, second the thing to leave out; order matches the English. ___なしで is an equally common alternative to 抜きで. A preference, not an allergy statement.

Literally 'Is it OK if (I) ___ here?' The blank holds the particle after ここ plus a て-form verb, because the particle changes: に for where you put yourself or your car (ここに座って, ここに停めて), で for actions done here (ここで写真を撮って). Not a noun slot.
Literally 'I am searching for ___.' The noun goes in directly; Japanese drops 'my/the/a'.
Literally 'Is ___ included?' Same shape as the vetted tip_included. ___付きですか？ ('does it come with ___') is also very common for meals at hotels.

Literally 'Where can (I) ___?' The blank holds the object, its particle and a potential-form verb stem (切符を買え, タクシーに乗れ, 両替でき), so it is not a noun slot. Putting the thing first as a topic (切符はどこで買えますか？) is equally natural.

word_beach.qa: 海 (sea) is also commonly used for 'the beach'.

word_city_centre.qa: Understood as 'downtown', but Japanese speakers usually name the district or main station (e.g. 新宿, 博多駅) rather than 'city centre'.

word_ticket_office.qa: At JR stations the staffed ticket office is みどりの窓口.

word_tea.qa: お茶 is usually green tea; black tea is 紅茶 (koh-chah).

word_bag.qa: かばん = one's own bag (belongings sense). A shopping/carrier bag is 袋 (foo-koo-roh).

word_receipt.qa: A formal receipt for expenses is 領収書 (ryoh-shoo-shoh).

word_milk.qa: SAFETY. Literally 'cow's milk'. ミルク is also used (e.g. for coffee).

word_nuts.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'nuts' (loanword). Standard; covers tree nuts generally. Peanuts are a separate word (ピーナッツ / 落花生).

word_gluten.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'gluten' (loanword). Less widely understood than 小麦 (koh-moo-gee, wheat), which is the allergen Japanese food labels list. Consider teaching 小麦 alongside it.

word_shellfish.target: 甲殻類・貝類・イカ・タコ
word_shellfish.reading: こうかくるい・かいるい・いか・たこ
word_shellfish.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'crustaceans' (shrimp, crab, lobster): the standard allergy term. Molluscs (clams, oysters, scallops) are 貝類 (kai-roo-ee); English 'shellfish' covers both. Labels list えび (shrimp) and かに (crab). [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]

word_meat.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'meat'. Does not include fish or fish stock (dashi).

word_dairy.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'milk products'. Same word as the existing dairy card.

word_peanuts.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'peanuts' (loanword). Food labels use 落花生 (rak-kah-say).

word_phone.qa: Short for 携帯電話 (mobile phone). スマホ (smartphone) is equally common.

word_ticket.qa: 切符 is a transport ticket; for events, チケット.

word_four.qa: し (shee) is the other reading; よん is safer in speech.

word_seven.qa: しち (shee-chee) is the other reading; なな is clearer in speech.

word_open.qa: Spoken form ('it's open'). Shop signs say 営業中 (ay-gyoh-choo).

word_closed.qa: Spoken form ('it's closed'). Signs say 準備中 (preparing) or 定休日 (regular day off).

is_there_nearby.pronunciation_easy: koh-noh chee-kah-koo nee toh-ee-reh wah ah-ree-mahs-kah

is_there_nearby.target: この近くに薬局はありますか？
is_there_nearby.reading: このちかくにやっきょくはありますか？
is_there_nearby.pronunciation_easy: koh-noh chee-kah-koo nee yak-kyoh-koo wah ah-ree-mahs-kah
is_there_nearby.qa: ドラッグストア (drugstore) is also common and often what you will find.

is_there_nearby.target: この近くにATMはありますか？
is_there_nearby.reading: このちかくにえーてぃーえむはありますか？
is_there_nearby.pronunciation_easy: koh-noh chee-kah-koo nee eh-tee-eh-moo wah ah-ree-mahs-kah

is_there_nearby.target: この近くにスーパーはありますか？
is_there_nearby.reading: このちかくにすーぱーはありますか？
is_there_nearby.pronunciation_easy: koh-noh chee-kah-koo nee soo-pah wah ah-ree-mahs-kah

pay_with.reading: げんきんではらえますか？
すまほではらえますか？
pay_with.qa: Understood, but staff may ask which method (Apple Pay, IC card, QR payment like PayPay); naming it is clearer.

can_you.target: 紙に書いてもらえますか？
can_you.reading: かみにかいてもらえますか？
can_you.qa: Literally 'Could you write it on paper for me?' 紙に is added for clarity; 書いてもらえますか？ alone also works, e.g. when handing over your phone.

like_without.target: コーヒーをミルク抜きでお願いします。
like_without.reading: こーひーをみるくぬきでおねがいします。
like_without.pronunciation_easy: koh-hee oh mee-roo-koo noo-kee deh oh-neh-guy-shee-mahs
like_without.qa: ブラックでお願いします ('Black, please') is the shorter everyday way.

like_without.target: 紅茶を砂糖抜きでお願いします。
like_without.reading: こうちゃをさとうぬきでおねがいします。
like_without.pronunciation_easy: koh-chah oh sah-toh noo-kee deh oh-neh-guy-shee-mahs
like_without.qa: 紅茶 = black (Western-style) tea; Japanese green tea (お茶) is unsweetened anyway.

like_without.target: お水を氷抜きでお願いします。
like_without.reading: おみずをこおりぬきでおねがいします。
like_without.pronunciation_easy: oh-mee-zoo oh koh-ree noo-kee deh oh-neh-guy-shee-mahs

can_i_here.target: ここに座ってもいいですか？
can_i_here.reading: ここにすわってもいいですか？
can_i_here.pronunciation_easy: koh-koh nee soo-waht-teh moh ee-ee des-kah

can_i_here.target: ここに車を停めてもいいですか？
can_i_here.reading: ここにくるまをとめてもいいですか？
can_i_here.pronunciation_easy: koh-koh nee koo-roo-mah oh toh-meh-teh moh ee-ee des-kah
can_i_here.qa: Literally 'May I stop my car here?': the everyday way. ここに駐車してもいいですか？ is more formal; for a bicycle, 車 becomes 自転車.

can_i_here.target: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか？
can_i_here.reading: ここでしゃしんをとってもいいですか？
can_i_here.pronunciation_easy: koh-koh deh shah-sheen oh toht-teh moh ee-ee des-kah

can_i_here.target: ここでスマホを充電してもいいですか？
can_i_here.reading: ここですまほをじゅうでんしてもいいですか？
can_i_here.pronunciation_easy: koh-koh deh soo-mah-hoh oh joo-den shee-teh moh ee-ee des-kah

looking_for.target: 泊まっているホテルを探しています。
looking_for.reading: とまっているほてるをさがしています。
looking_for.pronunciation_easy: toh-maht-teh ee-roo hoh-teh-roo oh sah-gah-shee-teh ee-mahs
looking_for.qa: Literally 'I'm looking for the hotel I'm staying at.' Japanese does not say 'my hotel'; adding the hotel name is even clearer.

looking_for.reading: いりぐちをさがしています。

looking_for.target: レストランを探しています。
looking_for.reading: れすとらんをさがしています。
でぐちをさがしています。

is_included.target: 朝食は含まれていますか？
is_included.reading: ちょうしょくはふくまれていますか？
is_included.qa: 朝食付きですか？ ('Does it come with breakfast?') is equally common at hotels.
Literally 'Is it tax-inclusive?': what people actually say about prices. 税金は含まれていますか？ is understood but wordier. Prices in Japan are usually shown tax-included.

is_included.reading: わいふぁいはふくまれていますか？
is_included.qa: Wi-Fi is usually free in hotels; Wi-Fiは無料ですか？ ('Is Wi-Fi free?') may be the more natural question.

is_included.target: 荷物の料金は含まれていますか？
is_included.reading: にもつのりょうきんはふくまれていますか？
is_included.pronunciation_easy: nee-moh-tsoo noh ryoh-keen wah foo-koo-mah-reh-teh ee-mahs-kah
is_included.qa: Literally 'Is the luggage fee included?' Added 料金 (fee) so it reads as a fare question; for flights, 預け荷物 (checked baggage) is the specific term. Not sure this is the most natural phrasing.

where_can_i.target: どこで切符を買えますか？
where_can_i.reading: どこできっぷをかえますか？
where_can_i.qa: 切符 = train/bus tickets; for events use チケット.

where_can_i.target: どこでタクシーに乗れますか？
where_can_i.reading: どこでたくしーにのれますか？
where_can_i.qa: Literally 'Where can I board a taxi?' タクシー乗り場はどこですか？ ('Where is the taxi stand?') is the most common way to ask.

where_can_i.target: どこで両替できますか？
where_can_i.reading: どこでりょうがえできますか？

where_can_i.target: どこでSIMカードを買えますか？
where_can_i.reading: どこでしむかーどをかえますか？
where_can_i.pronunciation_easy: doh-koh deh shee-moo kah-doh oh kah-eh-mahs-kah

for_here_or_to_go.target: 店内でお召し上がりですか、お持ち帰りですか？
for_here_or_to_go.reading: てんないでおめしあがりですか、おもちかえりですか？
for_here_or_to_go.pronunciation_easy: ten-nai deh oh-meh-shee-ah-gah-ree des-kah, oh-moh-chee-kah-eh-ree des-kah

anything_else.target: ご注文は以上でよろしいですか？
anything_else.reading: ごちゅうもんはいじょうでよろしいですか？
anything_else.pronunciation_easy: goh-choo-mon wah ee-joh deh yoh-roh-shee des-kah
anything_else.qa: Literally 'Is that everything for your order?': what staff actually say.

inside_or_outside.target: 中の席と外の席、どちらがよろしいですか？
inside_or_outside.reading: なかのせきとそとのせき、どちらがよろしいですか？
inside_or_outside.pronunciation_easy: nah-kah noh seh-kee toh soh-toh noh seh-kee, doh-chee-rah gah yoh-roh-shee des-kah
inside_or_outside.qa: Literally 'Inside seats or outside seats, which would you prefer?' Outdoor seating is less common in Japan; some places say 店内とテラス席.

have_booking.target: ご予約はされていますか？
have_booking.reading: ごよやくはされていますか？
have_booking.qa: ご予約はございますか？ is an equally common, more formal variant.

next_stop.qa: Bus recording after someone presses the stop button: 'Stopping at the next stop.' Train announcements instead say 次は___です (next is ___). Reviewer: confirm this is the best fit for 'Next stop.'

one_moment.reading: しょうしょうおまちください。

what_size.target: サイズはおいくつですか？
what_size.reading: さいずはおいくつですか？
what_size.qa: Clothing/shoe size. At a café, staff ask サイズはいかがなさいますか？ instead.

receipt_question.target: レシートはご入用ですか？
receipt_question.reading: れしーとはごいりようですか？
receipt_question.qa: Several variants are common: レシートはご利用ですか？, レシートはいりますか？ Note レシートはよろしいですか？ usually means 'You don't need a receipt, right?'

how_would_you_like_it.target: 今日はどうなさいますか？
how_would_you_like_it.reading: きょうはどうなさいますか？
how_would_you_like_it.qa: Literally 'What will you have done today?': the usual salon opener.
